# Skills and technical experience

My profile is deliberately multidisciplinary. The categories below describe methods and technologies used in different contexts; they do not imply identical depth or recency across every item. Concrete public evidence is linked wherever it exists. Industrial work that cannot be disclosed is described at a high level without exposing proprietary artefacts.

## Applied mathematics and scientific modelling

- Partial differential equations and applied mathematics
- Numerical simulation and reduced-order modelling
- Fluid mechanics, atmospheric dispersion, and environmental modelling
- Scientific reasoning: assumptions, model identification, approximation, and interpretation

**Evidence:** [Reduced-Order Modelling of Dispersion (2008)](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-1-4020-8758-5_14) and [Similitude généralisée et modélisation géométrique à complexité réduite (2006)](https://comptes-rendus.academie-sciences.fr/mecanique/articles/10.1016/j.crme.2006.06.007/).

**Technology context:** Fortran and SURFEX–TEB in research-oriented modelling.

## Statistics, Data Science, and machine learning

- Data analysis and statistical reasoning
- Classical machine learning
- Experiment design, model comparison, and benchmark evaluation
- Classification metrics, threshold analysis, and error analysis
- Python development and industrialisation

**Professional context:** five years of Data Science work in the Qlik/Talend lab. This includes work on data/statistics, ML, experiments, benchmarks, and evaluation. Specific methods should be assessed against project-level evidence rather than inferred from the job-family label alone.

## LLMs, NLP, and generative AI

- Evaluation of approaches for detecting unsupported or hallucinated model outputs
- Fact-checking and LLM-evaluation approaches
- Benchmark metric calculation and aggregation
- Threshold trade-offs and error analysis
- LLM/NLP and generative-AI experimentation

**Public evidence and limits:** the industrial hallucination benchmark is described in [Projects and research](projects.qmd) as a confidential case study. No private repository, source code, internal data, or implementation-specific architecture is linked.

## Software engineering and product development

- Python — practical experience in Data Science, evaluation tooling, and public software
- Java and Spring Boot — enterprise/backend application context
- Scala — enterprise software context
- JavaScript and ActionScript — application/front-end context
- PHP and front-end development
- BPM / business-process workflows
- AWS, Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker, and Kubernetes — cloud and AI-platform context
- Software design, modularity, testing, integration, and maintainability

**Public implementation example:** [Wiki Knowledge](https://github.com/JM-Brun/wiki-knowledge), a Python package for source ingestion, structured knowledge organisation, validation, and lexical search. Its current vector-search path falls back to BM25; it is not yet embedding-based semantic retrieval.

## Adapting across environments

The experience spans research-laboratory work, startup/product development, ESN consulting, and software-vendor contexts. The common skill is adapting methods and implementation choices to different constraints: scientific validity, user needs, system integration, maintainability, and operational delivery.

For detailed chronology and official role titles, see [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/brunjm/).
